items.action: 1. New todo_sync/ids.py (imports TodoSyncError from errors, never from the package): PREFIX = 'todo-', ALPHABET = '23456789abcdefghjkmnpqrstuvwxyz', CODE_LENGTH = 4; ID_RE, the word-bounded lowercase id with lookaheads requiring at least one digit and one letter; LEGACY_RE = \bTODO-[0-9]{3,}\b (copied from retire.py:25, whose own ID_RE stays until RSH-1); MIGRATE_HINT = 'the catalog still uses rank-tied TODO-NNN ids; run todo_sync.py migrate-ids --dry-run, then without --dry-run'. Functions: is_id(text) (fullmatch); is_legacy(catalog) (any item id fullmatching LEGACY_RE); taken_ids(catalog) (item ids plus retired_ids); new_id(taken, rng=None) (draws CODE_LENGTH rng.choice(ALPHABET) characters, redraws until is_id and not taken; default random.SystemRandom()); canonical(raw) (strip whitespace and one trailing ',' or ';', lower-case, add the prefix when missing; None unless is_id); mentions(text, ids) (the ids from `ids`, in their order, that `text` names case-insensitively on word bounds: the one matcher retire, split and the companion scans share); resolve_ids(catalog, raws) (canonical ids in input order without repeats, or one TodoSyncError joining every problem with '; ': a raw that reads as an old id (TODO-007, 007 or 7) reads 'TODO-007 is a rank-tied id from before migrate-ids: it meant todo-xxxx (<the live item's title>) as of <legacy_ids.migrated>; older references may name another item', with '(retired)' in place of the title when the id is in retired_ids, or 'TODO-007 is a rank-tied id from before migrate-ids: no legacy_ids entry'; an empty list 'name at least one TODO id'; a retired code 'todo-xxxx was retired', or 'todo-xxxx was split into todo-a, todo-b' when split_ids holds it; unknown codes 'no such item(s) in the catalog: ...'; anything else 'not a TODO id: ... (use todo-k7qf or k7qf)'); require_stable(catalog, verb) raises TodoSyncError(f'{verb}: {MIGRATE_HINT}') on a legacy catalog.

items.title: Catalog format: schema, fixtures, T1 and T6, init
items.action: 1. Schema: $defs.todo_id takes the stable pattern ^todo-(?=[2-9a-hjkmnp-z]*[2-9])(?=[2-9a-hjkmnp-z]*[a-hjkmnp-z])[2-9a-hjkmnp-z]{4}$ with a description (random, stable, never reused; order lives in rank); new $defs.legacy_todo_id ^TODO-[0-9]{3,}$; optional top-level retired_ids (array of todo_id, uniqueItems), legacy_ids (object, additionalProperties false, required migrated (format date) and map (object, propertyNames legacy_todo_id, values todo_id)) and split_ids (object, propertyNames todo_id, values arrays of todo_id with minItems 2 and uniqueItems: the parts a split gave a retired id, in spec order); rewrite the descriptions at :5 (T6 checks unique ids absent from retired_ids and the split_ids records, not TODO-<rank>), :62, :647 and :652. 2. plugins/harness/schemas/README.md:180-184 says the same. 3. rules_todo.py: T1 drops the pattern errors whose instance fullmatches ids.LEGACY_RE when ids.is_legacy(catalog), leaving the catalog to T6. T6 on a legacy catalog returns one error finding (message names migrate-ids, fix 'Run todo_sync.py migrate-ids --dry-run, then without --dry-run.') plus its duplicate-id findings, which migrate-ids needs cleared first; on a stable catalog it reports duplicate ids ('id X appears N times'), an item id listed in retired_ids ('id X is in retired_ids'), a split_ids key missing from retired_ids ('split id X is not in retired_ids'), a part that is neither an item nor retired ('split id X names part Y, neither an item nor retired'), and ranks that do not run 1..n in item order; the id == TODO-<rank> check (:142-144) goes. 4. scaffold.py: starter_catalog writes "retired_ids": [] after close_candidates; the notes sentence 'so ids and ranks are reproducible from the item fields alone' becomes 'so ranks are reproducible from the item fields alone; ids never change'. 5. Fixtures: copy tests/fixtures/todo_sync/TodoCatalog.min.json unchanged to TodoCatalog.legacy.json; in the min fixture rename TODO-001 -> todo-p4rs, TODO-002 -> todo-sp7t, TODO-003 -> todo-c4ch everywhere (ids, links, trackers, close candidates, prose) and add "retired_ids": []. 6. tests/lib/_todo_helpers.py: ID1, ID2, ID3 = the three fixture ids; LEGACY_CATALOG loaded from the legacy fixture, with the literal file name "TodoCatalog.legacy.json" in the code (tools/select_tests.py maps a fixture change to its readers only through that literal). 7. items.title: retire: record retired ids, re-rank, rewrite nothing
items.action: 1. retire.py imports the id module as `from harness_lib.todo_sync import ids as todo_ids` (retire_items and apply_retirement take a parameter named ids, which shadows a bare `ids` import). It deletes _rewrite_catalog and keeps ID_RE, _SHORT, todo_id, normalize_id, remap_text and companion_edits, which reshape.py imports until RSH-1 deletes them; retire's own paths stop calling them. 2. load_catalog(cfg, verb, stable=True) calls todo_ids.require_stable(data, verb) when stable is true (migrate-ids passes False). 3. retire_items(catalog, ids): require_stable; gone = todo_ids.resolve_ids; drop the items; unlink as today (_ordered, _drop_links); ranks 1..n in the kept order; append the retired ids, in catalog order, to catalog['retired_ids'] (created when absent); recount; dangling lists every catalog string naming a gone id through todo_ids.mentions (case-insensitive) as '<json path> names retired <id>', item paths reading 'items/<id>/...', skipping the top-level id records retired_ids, legacy_ids and split_ids; no other string changes. Retirement loses renames. 4. history_paths(cfg) -> repo-relative posix paths without a trailing '/': artifacts.plans, artifacts.reviews, artifacts.commit_messages, artifacts.summaries, artifacts.scratch, each artifacts.planning_prefixes entry, and todo.snapshots.dir when set. 5. companion_mentions(cfg, notes) -> '<rel>:<line> <note>' for each research-catalog or stub line naming an id in notes (todo_ids.mentions); nothing is rewritten. 6. git_grep(cfg, args) runs `git -C <root> grep <args>` (timeout 60 s) and returns its stdout lines; exit 1 means none; an OSError, a timeout or an exit of 2 or more raises TodoSyncError('git grep failed: <reason>') with the OSError text, 'timed out after 60 s', or git's first stderr line. other_references(cfg, ids) -> 'path:line:text' from git_grep with --untracked -n -I -i -F -w and one -e per id and no exclude pathspecs: lines under the catalog, the companions and history_paths are dropped in Python (a long pathspec list overruns the Windows command line); () when ids is empty or the project root holds no .git. 7. apply_retirement writes only the catalog (write_edits(cfg, text, {})), then scans; a TodoSyncError from other_references leaves references () and sets scan_error. RetireResult loses rewritten and gains scan_error: Optional[str] = None; summary_lines drops the renumbered and rewrote lines and prints 'reference scan failed: <scan_error>'. 8. RetireResult.dangling holds the catalog lines first, then companion_mentions ('<rel>:<line> names retired <id>'); summary_lines prints each as 'dangling: ...'.

items.title: migrate-ids: the one-time switch with a legacy map
items.action: New todo_sync/migrate.py (the id module as todo_ids). migrate_catalog(catalog, today, rng=None) -> Migration(catalog, mapping, unmapped): (a) refusals: no legacy item id and no legacy_ids, 'nothing to migrate: every item id is already stable'; duplicate legacy item ids, 'duplicate legacy id(s): TODO-002, ...; give each item its own id first'; a legacy item id already a key of legacy_ids.map, '<id> is already in legacy_ids (migrated <date>); an older harness may have renumbered the catalog: restore it from git'. (b) Each legacy item id, in item order, draws todo_ids.new_id over the taken ids; with rng None each draw is seeded from sha256 of '<old id>\0<title>' (random.Random over the first 8 bytes), so two checkouts of one catalog, and a dry run and its real run, give the same map; a passed rng is used as is. (c) The full map is the stored legacy_ids.map plus the new entries; every catalog string outside legacy_ids is rewritten through it in one pass (no chained renames). A link-list entry (depends_on, unblocks, child_todo_ids, related_todo_ids) with no mapping is dropped and listed '<json path of the list> dropped TODO-NNN, no live item'; any other string keeps it, listed '<json path> names TODO-NNN, no live item' (item paths read items/<new id>/...). A link list sorted before the rewrite is sorted after it. (d) retired_ids is set to [] when absent; legacy_ids = {migrated: the stored date, else today; map: the stored entries plus the new ones}; mapping holds only the new entries (empty on a rerun). apply_migration(cfg, dry_run=False, exclude=(), today=None, rng=None) -> MigrateResult(migration, rewritten ((rel, hits), ...), unmapped ('rel:line names TODO-NNN'), skipped ((rel, reason), ...), schema_problem: Optional[str]): loads with load_catalog(cfg, 'migrate-ids', stable=False); the files are the companions plus retire.git_grep(--untracked -l -I -E 'TODO-[0-9]{3,}') (a git failure raises before anything is written) minus the catalog, the configured catalog schema (cfg.todo.catalog_schema), retire.history_paths and every exclude; an exclude matches by path component after posix() and dropping a trailing '/' ('vendor' skips vendor/x.md, never vendored.md). Every file is read and strictly decoded before any write; a file that is not UTF-8 is skipped ('not UTF-8'); rewrites go through the full map and keep bytes and line endings; old ids with no mapping stay and are listed. When cfg.todo.catalog_schema is set, the migrated catalog is validated against that schema (its declared draft, as T1 does); a failure sets schema_problem '<schema rel> rejects the migrated catalog (<first error, cut to 200 characters>); replace it with the harness catalogs/TodoCatalog.schema.json or update its id pattern, then rerun'. A dry run reports it; a real run raises it before writing. A real run writes the catalog first (dump_like, write_atomic, only when its text changed), then each file through the module-level write_file(path, data); a file that fails raises TodoSyncError naming every file not written ('not written: a, b; rerun migrate-ids to finish through the stored map'). A dry run writes nothing. summary_lines(result, dry_run): '[would migrate|migrated] N item(s) to stable ids', one 'id TODO-NNN -> todo-xxxx' line per new entry, '[would rewrite|rewrote] <rel> (<n> reference(s))', 'unmapped: ...' (capped at REFERENCE_CAP), 'skipped: <rel> (<reason>)', 'schema: <schema_problem>', 'history left as written: <paths>', and on a real run 'next: todo_sync.py render, then todo_sync.py check'.

decisions.question: What does a TODO item id look like once it no longer follows rank?

options.summary: TODO-<rank>, renumbered on every structural edit (today)
todo- plus 4 random characters, collision-checked
letters from a stored counter (todo-aaf)
creation date plus a count (todo-261109-2)

decisions.rationale: Issue 243: renumbering broke references outside the rewrite set. Counter and date ids collide when two worktrees add items at once; a random code does not, and carries no position.

decisions.question: How is a retired id kept from being drawn again?

options.summary: collision check against live ids only
catalog-level retired_ids list; new draws skip live and retired

decisions.rationale: A reused id makes every stale reference point at an unrelated item, the failure issue 243 reports; the list grows by one per retirement.

decisions.question: Which ids do the parts of a split get?

options.summary: the first part inherits the original id
every part gets a new id; the original is retired and its prose listed

decisions.rationale: Inheriting the id guesses which part a reference meant; a listed dangling id is honest.

decisions.question: How far does the one-time switch-over rewrite old TODO-NNN references?

options.summary: every file naming an old id, history included
live files only; plans, reviews, snapshots and commit messages stay as history; the old->new map is stored

decisions.rationale: History records describe the catalog when written and some are already stale; rewriting them with the current map turns stale references into confidently wrong ones.

decisions.question: Where does the old->new map live?

options.summary: top-level legacy_ids object in the catalog
a map file beside the catalog

decisions.rationale: Schema-validated, travels with the catalog, needs no new path or config key.

decisions.question: Upper- or lower-case prefix and code?

options.summary: TODO-K7QF
todo-k7qf

decisions.rationale: Developer's call; also keeps new ids disjoint from the TODO-NNN pattern and from TODO: comments. Commands accept any case.

decisions.question: What happens to a catalog that still holds TODO-NNN ids?

options.summary: check reports one T6 finding naming migrate-ids; retire, split, add and refresh refuse
schema and T6 report every id

decisions.rationale: One actionable line instead of a capped flood of pattern errors.

decisions.question: Which marketplace release does this change suggest?

options.summary: harness 0.64.0 -> 0.65.0, extend docs/RELEASES/v0.7.0.md
the catalog format change counts as breaking across the marketplace

decisions.rationale: Developer's call 2026-11-09: the switch is one command with a dry run and nothing is renamed or removed; harness 0.64.0 -> 0.65.0 joins the pending v0.7.0 notes.

decisions.question: Which codes may the generator draw?

options.summary: any 4 characters of the 31-character alphabet
at least one digit and at least one letter

decisions.rationale: Without a digit the generator can draw todo-sync, a name already in use; without a letter a code reads as a number.

decisions.question: How does migrate-ids draw the new ids?

options.summary: each legacy item's draw seeded from its old id and title
SystemRandom, as add and split draw

decisions.rationale: Review A4: two worktrees that each run the switch must agree, and the dry run must show the ids the real run writes; add and split keep the random draw of D1.

decisions.question: Where does a split record its parts?

options.summary: top-level split_ids: retired id -> part ids, in spec order
retired_ids alone; the parts appear only in that run's report

decisions.rationale: Review A9: references the scan cannot see (issue comments, notes, other branches) still resolve: resolve_ids answers 'todo-sp7t was split into todo-a, todo-b'.

decisions.question: What does migrate-ids do on a catalog that already holds legacy_ids?

options.summary: rewrite remaining live references through the stored map; new legacy ids join it; a key already mapped refuses
'nothing to migrate' once the items are stable

decisions.rationale: Reviews A1, A5, B5: a partial write, a git failure or a branch merged after the switch leaves TODO-NNN references only the stored map resolves; a key already mapped means an older harness renumbered the catalog, which a fresh map would hide.

decisions.question: Which files outside the catalog does migrate-ids rewrite by default?

options.summary: every live file; history, --exclude paths and the catalog schema skipped
catalog and companions only; other files only with --include

decisions.rationale: Developer's call 2026-11-09 (one last rewrite of every reference); review A6's opt-in default declined: the dry run lists every file first, --exclude (by path component) removes any, and the catalog schema file is never rewritten.

decisions.question: When does this repository's own catalog switch?

options.summary: after harness 0.65.0 is released and installed wherever todo_sync runs here
on this branch, before the release

decisions.rationale: Review A1: sessions here run the published plugin, whose add and refresh renumber stable ids back to TODO-<rank>; the switch waits for the release (deferred_to_future_plans).
